scope: Replace the generic post-hoc rider paragraph in WIN-012.detail_verdict_text with a WIN-012-specific paragraph that names the actual failure mode: 'ratio of noncoincident observables, applied as a universal constant by fiat'. The generic rider currently claims the dome 'derives [κ] from its own geometric or symbolic parameters (disc radius, firmament height, chosen symmetry axis, or similar)' — but the first paragraph of WIN-012.detail_verdict_text itself states the actual failure mode: 'The coupling constant is a post-hoc assembly of two measurements from different eclipses, different locations, and different physical quantities — not a prediction from dome geometry.' The rider directly contradicts the upstream argument. This EXP swaps the rider for a paragraph that matches the actual failure mode while preserving the Self-Contradicted verdict and the dome-author-definition + Part 3.1b cross-reference closing. Opening first paragraph is preserved verbatim — only the second paragraph (boilerplate) is replaced. Single-patch deep-attack-by-naming EXP.

analyst_assessment: The c3 reviewer's per-WIN assessment of WIN-012 anticipated 'WIN-012 likely involves a different failure mode (assembly-from-eclipse-fits)'. This is correct: κ = 1.67 nT/µGal is the ratio of −10.9 nT (BOU 2017 eclipse magnetometer) and −6.5 µGal (Mohe 1997 eclipse gravimeter) — two observations from different events, locations, instrument classes, separated by 20 years, with no co-located simultaneous measurement of both quantities. This is not 'the dome derives a value from disc_radius and the disc_radius was itself fit to globe data' (the rider's template). It is 'the dome picks two values from a menu of observations and ratios them.' The replacement paragraph names this failure mode 'ratio of noncoincident observables, applied as a universal constant by fiat,' and preempts the defender objection 'every empirical constant is a ratio of two measurements' by listing what a physical constant requires that κ lacks: (a) co-located simultaneous measurement, (b) falsifiable forward predictions, (c) updating when subsequent measurements invalidate the ratio. The dome's WIN-013/WIN-014 nulls (Membach 1999, Chinese SG 2009) furnish the (c) point directly from the dome's own published data. The replacement does not soften the Self-Contradicted verdict; it sharpens it. Verdict unchanged.
kernel_of_truth: The dome correctly identifies that the BOU 2017 eclipse magnetic perturbation and the Mohe 1997 eclipse gravity perturbation are both real measurements (BOU is a legitimate USGS magnetometer station; Mohe is a real Chinese gravimetry site). Reaching for a universal coupling constant between magnetic and gravitational fields is the right kind of ambition for a candidate new physics — IF such a coupling existed and were universal, it would be a profound discovery analogous to fine-structure or gravitational constants. The replacement paragraph acknowledges this theoretical posture explicitly ('reaching for one is the right kind of ambition for a new theory') before showing why the execution fails: κ is not actually a measured constant; it is a ratio of two unrelated observations declared structural by fiat, retained even after later measurements null the denominator, and re-applied to new events post-hoc. The kernel is bounded (ambition is right; execution never establishes the constant) and the takedown follows immediately.

patches.old_string: Independent of the scientific critique above, this claim also fails our post-hoc test. The numerical value is one the dome framework derives from its own geometric or symbolic parameters (disc radius, firmament height, chosen symmetry axis, or similar), and the "confirmation" consists of matching that derivation to a globe-measured value — which, because the dome parameters were themselves fit to globe data (see Kill-Shot #1 and Part 2b), is circular. There is no pre-registration of the derivation in a venue that timestamps independently of the author, and the dome monitor script (where one exists) encodes the expected value in the same commit as the comparison. Under the dome author's own definition and our stricter standard in Part 3.1b, this is retrodiction, not prediction.
patches.new_string: Independent of the scientific critique above, this claim fails our prediction test via a stronger failure mode than ordinary post-hoc retrodiction. The kernel the dome gets right is the theoretical posture: a universal coupling constant between magnetic and gravitational fields — if it existed — would be a profound physical discovery, and reaching for one is the right kind of ambition for a new theory. The execution, however, never establishes the constant the dome claims to have measured. κ = 1.67 nT/µGal is computed as a ratio of two observations from entirely separate events: the numerator (−10.9 nT) is a BOU magnetometer reading during the August 2017 North American eclipse; the denominator (−6.5 µGal) is a Mohe spring-gravimeter reading during the March 1997 eclipse — different decade, different hemisphere, different instrument class, no co-located simultaneous measurement of both quantities. The dome then treats this ratio as a structural coupling and applies it across physically distinct regimes — 2017 eclipse ionospheric perturbation, 1997 eclipse gravity transient, and the 2003 Halloween G5 storm ring-current event (raw-text/08-live-power.txt line 226; raw-text/01-home.txt line 32) — without publishing any derivation from disc_radius (20,015 km), H(r) = 8,537 × exp(−r/8,619), or any dome geometry parameter that explains why a single coupling constant should hold across these regimes. So this is not derive-then-match: it is ratio of noncoincident observables, applied as a universal constant by fiat. A defender will note that every empirical constant is a ratio of two measurements — and we grant that — but a physical constant requires (a) measurements of the same system at the same time, (b) falsifiable predictions about future measurements, (c) updating when subsequent measurements (the dome's own WIN-013 Membach 1999 and WIN-014 Chinese SG 2009, both 0.0 µGal) yield results that invalidate the original ratio. The dome's κ fails all three: numerator and denominator are non-coincident, the application scope is unspecified, and when the gravity-side measurement returns to null, the dome retains κ = 1.67 and reaches for the 2003 storm as a new confirmation event post-hoc. Until the dome publishes a derivation of κ from disc geometry — or restricts its scope to events where both quantities have been co-measured — WIN-012 is event-shopping, not measurement. Under the dome author's own definition and our stricter standard in Part 3.1b, this is not prediction.

anticipated_objections.objection: The first paragraph of WIN-012.detail_verdict_text already says 'not a prediction from dome geometry' — the new rider is just rephrasing what's already there.
anticipated_objections.response: The new rider does more than rephrase. It (a) names the failure mode explicitly ('ratio of noncoincident observables, applied as a universal constant by fiat') so future cross-WIN audits can recognize the same pattern, (b) acknowledges the kernel of truth (universal EM-gravity coupling would be profound; reaching for one is the right ambition) — the upstream paragraph does not, (c) preempts the defender's 'every empirical constant is a ratio' objection with a three-prong rebuttal, and (d) ties the failure to the dome's own WIN-013/WIN-014 nulls and the 2003 Halloween storm event addition as the concrete evidence of post-hoc event-shopping. The upstream paragraph is a verdict-summary tagline; the new rider is the structural argument. Both are needed.

anticipated_objections.objection: Acknowledging that 'reaching for a universal coupling constant ... is the right kind of ambition' gives the dome author too much credit and could be quoted out of context.
anticipated_objections.response: Kernel-of-truth acknowledgement is the standard discipline (analyst.md 'YOUR MOST IMPORTANT DIRECTIVE'). The acknowledgement is technically accurate and bounded: it praises the posture, not the execution; the next sentence is 'The execution, however, never establishes the constant the dome claims to have measured.' EXP-330 made the same trade on WIN-056 (acknowledged H(r) construction as 'sophisticated curve-fitting' then immediately said 'The execution, however, never closes the loop'). The pattern is intentional — it forces the defender to engage with the structural argument rather than dismissing the critique as a snipe.

anticipated_objections.objection: WIN-030 and WIN-069 still carry the same generic rider — shouldn't this EXP also patch them?
anticipated_objections.response: No, per the c3 WIN-056 reviewer's explicit anti-sweep guidance: 'EACH should be inspected on its own merits — for these WINs the rider may legitimately fit... a mechanical sweep is explicitly NOT warranted.' WIN-030 (elliptical disc geometry: R²/AIC failure mode) and WIN-069 (Australia road scaffold: V13 parameters fit to π×R_Earth) may have failure modes that the generic rider matches more closely than WIN-012's does. WIN-030 in particular involves dome-fit parameters used to fit globe data — that IS the rider's pattern. The decider should queue WIN-030 and WIN-069 as separate analyst per-WIN reviews. This EXP scopes to WIN-012 only — the most clearly mismatched of the three (where the rider directly contradicts the immediately preceding sentence).

anticipated_objections.objection: The replacement makes the verdict-text longer — is the cost-benefit favorable for a verdict field that's already heavy with detail_evidence?
anticipated_objections.response: WIN-012.detail_evidence is 5697 chars (the full structural argument). detail_verdict_text grows from 1351→~3242 chars — still ~57% the size of detail_evidence and well below WIN-056's 2631-char detail_verdict_text after EXP-330. The growth carries new content (failure-mode naming, kernel acknowledgement, defender preemption, three-prong rebuttal) — not redundancy. Verdict-text is read first by skim-readers who don't open the detail_evidence accordion; making it carry the structural argument is the design intent.

anticipated_objections.objection: If the dome later publishes a derivation of κ from disc geometry, the new rider would need updating — wasn't the old rider's vagueness a feature?
anticipated_objections.response: The new rider explicitly invites this fix: 'Until the dome publishes a derivation of κ from disc geometry — or restricts its scope to events where both quantities have been co-measured — WIN-012 is event-shopping, not measurement.' If the dome publishes such a derivation, the rider would update — exactly as we'd want. The old rider's vagueness was a bug, not a feature: it falsely claimed the dome HAD derived κ from disc geometry, which contradicted the upstream argument and would have been a hostage to defender objection ('show me where I said disc_radius and firmament_height derive κ — you can't, because I never did'). The new rider is more precise and more falsifiable as a critique.
